dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently implement a code security audit toolkit: OWASP checks, dependency audits, secret detection, SSL/TLS checks, AI-agent security patterns, report generation, and CI templates all fit the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill is broad within security-audit use cases and directs shell-based scanning of a project, but that is disclosed and central to its function rather than hidden or unrelated authority.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope

dimensions.detail: There is no hidden installer or remote bootstrapper. CI templates install common security tools from package registries, which is expected for dependency and security scanning workflows.

dimensions.detail: Most reads are scoped to PROJECT_DIR, but the full permission audit checks ~/.ssh directory permissions and secret scans may reveal matching lines in output, especially with verbose mode or CI logs.

dimensions.detail: The skill does not automatically persist, escalate privileges, or modify other skills. It includes an optional pre-commit hook example and can write a report to a user-selected output path.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Shell commands such as grep, npm audit, openssl, curl, and filesystem inspection are expected for a local security-audit toolkit; the manifest and documentation disclose the relevant tools.
[SDI-1] expected: The ~/.ssh check reaches outside the project, but the script only checks directory permissions and the behavior is shown in the file-permission audit documentation; this is a user-awareness caveat, not evidence of secret reading or exfiltration.
[SQP-1] expected: The activation language is broad, but it remains focused on security audits, vulnerability scanning, secret detection, OWASP compliance, AI/LLM app security, and security reviews.
[TM1] unexpected: The optional pre-commit hook example prints a --no-verify bypass hint, which is weak security guidance, but it is not automatically installed and does not create hidden evasion behavior.
llm.guidance: Install this only when you want a local security audit. Run it in a private workspace or controlled CI job, because secret-detection matches can appear in terminal output or logs. Set PROJECT_DIR deliberately for tight scope, review the ~/.ssh permission check if host-level checks are unwanted, and avoid using the optional --no-verify bypass guidance as part of a real enforcement workflow.
llm.summary: This is a coherent local security-audit skill, with expected scanning behavior and a few usage caveats around secret output and host permission checks.
